title: SANReN's 100 Gbps Data Transfer Service: Transferring data fast!
problem: South African researchers lack access to high-speed national data transfer infrastructure for large datasets. Separate deployment of DTNs and perfSONAR monitoring nodes incurs excessive hardware costs, maintenance overhead, and requires substantial rack space that many institutions cannot afford.
motivation: Supporting data-intensive research at South African institutions requires cost-effective shared national infrastructure since individual institutions cannot independently deploy high-performance data transfer capabilities.
method: SANReN deployed Data Transfer Nodes (computers that move large research datasets) capable of 100 Gbps speeds using Globus software at two locations—Cape Town and Johannesburg—connected by an upgraded high-speed network backbone. Instead of requiring separate machines for data transfer and network-performance monitoring (perfSONAR, a tool that watches how the network is performing), they built one combined system that does both jobs. This cuts equipment costs, reduces maintenance burden, and lets institutions with limited rack space actually participate in the national research network.
key_novelty: They built the first working shared national research infrastructure where a single Data Transfer Node and network-performance monitoring system (DTN/perfSONAR) serves multiple institutions, eliminating the need for separate specialized hardware.
contributions: 100 Gbps Data Transfer Node deployment across South African locations
Combined DTN/perfSONAR node architecture reducing infrastructure and operational costs
Achieved 4.78-5.48 GBps sustained transfer speeds (1TB in 3 minutes)
Validated international data transfer performance and demonstrated national-scale reliability
limitations: Paper does not discuss scalability beyond two nodes, international connectivity bottlenecks, or cost-benefit analysis compared to alternative data transfer approaches.
